title: What can you say about omega-3 fish oil (EPA and DHA) in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 6 wordings for omega-3 fish oil (EPA and DHA); the strongest is "Supports normal heart function and heart health" (strong, 250-5,000 mg EPA + DHA a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Lowers high triglycerides, or treats hypertriglyceridemia".

supported_wordings.wording: Supports normal heart function and heart health.
supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review at 250 mg a day, and listed by Health Canada from 200 mg a day.
supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: 250 mg EPA + DHA a day, and the consumer is told so. Health Canada: 200-5,000 mg a day. Adult maximum 5,000 mg a day.

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

supported_wordings.wording: Helps maintain normal blood triglyceride levels.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 1,000-5,000 mg a day, and ODS reports a large Cochrane review showing lower triglycerides.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 1,000-5,000 mg a day. ODS reports a 2020 Cochrane review in which 0.5 g to more than 5 g a day lowered triglycerides by about 15%.

sources.name: NIH ODS fact sheet: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (health professional)

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada and the EU accept maintenance wording, but ODS reports a trial in healthy older adults in which EPA + DHA did not change cognitive function.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 150-5,000 mg EPA + DHA a day including at least 100 mg DHA. EU: 250 mg DHA a day.

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims
NIH ODS fact sheet: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (health professional)

supported_wordings.where_sources_disagree: Health Canada (cognitive health and brain function) and the EU (maintenance of normal brain function) support the wording. ODS describes a 24-month trial in cognitively healthy adults aged 70-79 in which 500 mg DHA plus 200 mg EPA a day made no significant difference to cognitive function compared with placebo. Maintenance wording may hold; wording that promises better memory or thinking does not.

supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review; Health Canada lists eye development only for children.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: at least 250 mg DHA a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: 250 mg DHA a day, and the consumer is told so. Adult maximum for EPA + DHA is 5,000 mg a day (Health Canada).

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at EPA-rich doses; no other listed source covers this wording.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 1,500-5,000 mg EPA + DHA a day including at least 1,000 mg EPA.
supported_wordings.form: Fish oil providing EPA-rich EPA + DHA

supported_wordings.wording: Supports healthy development of the brain, eyes and nerves in children up to 12.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it for children; no other listed source covers this wording.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 200-2,000 mg EPA + DHA a day including at least 150 mg DHA, within the age-based maximums (1,500 mg a day at ages 1-8; 2,000 mg at ages 9-11).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers high triglycerides, or treats hypertriglyceridemia
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease (raised blood fats); the supported wording is maintaining normal levels.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Reduces the risk of heart disease or heart attack, outside FDA's qualified wording
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. The supported route is FDA's qualified claims, with their wording and conditions (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers blood pressure, or helps with hypertension, outside FDA's qualified wording
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. FDA's 2019 qualified claims set the wording and conditions.
Names a mental health disorder; the supported wording is healthy mood balance.
Names a disease. Health Canada lists this only alongside conventional therapy, at 2,800-5,000 mg a day.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Protects against dementia or Alzheimer's disease
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases; ODS reports no cognitive benefit in a trial in healthy older adults.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
